label: Standard of favouring: value ranking or end-realization ordering
resolution: The loss and arbitrariness bridges (MissingVerdictIsImpure, UnbackedVerdictIsImpure) measure a favouring profile against a standard, and their verdict on the disputed pair depends on which. STANDARD_OF_FAVOURING_1 (ValueStandardOrder): the betterness ranking read as value; with it a favouring determined to end content D misses a verdict wherever betterness varies within a D-class, and the good-tracking favouring tracks it exactly. STANDARD_OF_FAVOURING_2 (EndRealizationOrder): the end-realization ordering; with it the good-tracking favouring makes an unbacked verdict (c over d at cBetter on the control carrier) and the D-directed favouring tracks it exactly. The statements 720bccc2 and a141e6a8 and the registered argument b86a2364 use sense 1 only: their standard parameter is a value order v : ValueStandardOrder, whose relation v.better is the value ranking. The D-relative form is the generic MissingVerdictIsImpure and UnbackedVerdictIsImpure applied to an end-realization order's relation; it appears only in the Lean-only control standardRelativity and is not a corpus statement (standardControls row 6 is a value order whose relation coincides with end-realization, not sense 2). The two senses are distinct Lean types (ValueStandardOrder and EndRealizationOrder); the registered value-sense declarations MissingValueVerdictIsImpure, UnbackedValueVerdictIsImpure and BetternessVariesWithinEndClass take a ValueStandardOrder, so passing an end-realization order needs an explicit construction from its relation, which would be a sense bridge, and an unbridged mix fails to typecheck. The registered conclusion uses the value order's relation by explicit projection, because 7fca65ec's ranking parameter is untagged. No step passes between the senses: neither is defined from the other, and on the control carrier they differ at one verdict in genuine scenarios. Whether a single standard governs every favouring, and which, or whether each favouring is measured by the formal object of its kind of operation (so that the verdict on a root's favouring turns on whether it is a natural or a rational appetite), is the open question of docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'When is a restriction of content a limitation?'.
